purpose: Evaluator-only contrasts. Never include this file, kind labels or expected outcomes in reviewer context.

expect: Expose the fixed Sender dependency at construction using the established selection contract.
Preserve billingSender identity and singleton lifetime; no new interface twin or container.
Retain operation-data routing; Primary/Fallback cannot choose a sender per message.
Do not equate explicit channel keys with bean names or turn two closed cases into a plugin platform.
Identify the shared settings contract and compare supported ConfigurationProperties binding with repeated parsing.
Preserve endpoint/timeout keys, seconds, default 5, supported input rules and registration; a DurationUnit/default or compatible explicit conversion is needed, not an unchecked type substitution.
Retain the clear isolated Value contract unless a concrete burden is demonstrated.
No mandatory properties record, configuration wrapper or validation expansion.
Recognize the constructor-injection versus constructor-binding distinction before annotation removal.
Retain Autowired and the established bean binding path; do not force this dependency-bearing object into a record.
No unconditional proxyBeanMethods=false or Configuration removal while direct factory calls remain.
A justified parameter-injection alternative must retain bean names and shared object identity; mere annotation/line reduction is insufficient.
Identify the contract-free forwarding hop and simplify its actual caller path.
Retain the Spring Data interface's generated implementation contract; no blanket ban on repository/service interfaces.
Retain the existing application port and missing-customer vocabulary.
One implementation or a short method does not erase its independent consumer/adaptation contract.
Compare the custom import selector with ConditionalOnProperty for the same registration condition.
Retain the exact supported true/false/absent contract and eliminate redundant selector plumbing without introducing runtime dispatch.
Keep the documented auto-configuration back-off, name and ordering contract.
Do not replace MissingBean with Primary/Fallback or delete the annotation because there are no literal callers.
A named value-only business-date calculation can expose the existing rule within the operation.
Preserve the sampled instant/zone and effect order; no new Spring service, mapper platform, command hierarchy or domain requirements.
Retain the short application operation and transaction unit used by two consumers.
Do not inline into one HTTP adapter, require an interface or assume self-invoked annotated helpers create separate advice.
Express the two existing routes directly with supported MVC mappings rather than re-decoding the servlet path.
Preserve both paths, methods, media type and bodies; no new HTTP versioning or endpoint protocol.
Recognize RouterFunction as a native WebFlux mechanism, not a custom dispatcher.
Do not force annotation controllers, blocking calls or an architectural replacement.
Localize identical Missing-to-HTTP translation in a sufficient local handler or narrowly scoped advice.
Keep the code envelope and 404 response; no new generic reflection registry, global unrelated policy or domain HTTP exception.
Retain the versioned error envelope, header and advice scope.
ProblemDetail/ErrorResponse availability alone does not justify a wire change or merging independent error policies.
Retain the explicit MVC request-argument validation contract.
Do not conflate MethodArgumentNotValidException with WebExchangeBindException or method/AOP validation; no added constraints.
Use the supplied WebFlux argument-validation contract and existing error advice.
No MVC exception substitution, mandatory reactive redesign, block or subscribe insertion.
Preserve the managed object's identity and visible mutation.
Do not replace it with a new record/object or remove save solely from a dirty-checking argument; keep the established repository boundary.
Retain per-use provider resolution for request identity.
Do not cache one tenant in the singleton or invent a resource leak/race finding.
Identify the lifecycle-only registry burden and compare direct bean init/destroy callbacks for the same object and phases.
Do not migrate to ApplicationReadyEvent or a different SmartLifecycle phase merely because it is a framework feature; preserve external ownership if evidence changes.
Keep caller ownership of the client/session.
No try-with-resources in export, container lifecycle takeover or new bean registry.
Retain the explicit reactive transaction operator and consumer-owned subscription.
No subscribe/block, thread-bound transaction substitution or new scheduler as a readability remedy.
Name the id/name result to remove repeated positional decoding, with an exact supported constructor projection or identified provider mechanism.
Preserve query fields/order and consumers; a typed result is not an entity, and Java record support alone is not proof of arbitrary JPQL syntax.
Keep the entity/response distinction, entity identity/mutation and required provider constructor.
Do not merge DTO and entity, convert entity to record, or delete constructor/accessors from an empty literal search.
Recognize the explicitly supported Hibernate record embeddable, distinct from an entity.
Do not invent a no-arg requirement for that record or claim portable Persistence 3.2 support from this API 3.1 baseline.
Preserve the serializer/accessor contract or leave a version/consumer-dependent remedy unresolved.
No assumed current Boot/Jackson generation, record conversion or getter removal based solely on no local callers.
Retain the sufficient shared simple input shape.
No mandatory request/command/DTO twins or mapper for an unimplemented independent boundary.
Select profiles from the actual servlet handler and WebClient consumer; keep the normal base applicability plan.
Do not infer WebFlux server or JPA coverage from client/reactor dependencies; evidence of absence differs from missing evidence.
Record the unavailable framework/dependency baseline for version-specific advice without running Gradle or inventing versions from the JDK.
Retain the clear qualifiers; no unconditional Fallback/constructor-binding modernization or blanket incomplete verdict for unrelated resolved observations.
Honor API-only scope and explicit profile exclusions; do not claim full Spring/Java coverage.
Do not add Kotlin coverage, lifecycle, representation or a broad Spring agent.
The Spring profile cannot revive the disabled java.abstractions rule in the B policy scope.
Record a policy exclusion rather than a clean all-aspects result or missing execution; no namespace substitution.
